q: 1. Too much fineness of cement
explain: Very fine cement hydrates faster, generating more heat of hydration, which can lead to thermal cracking in concrete — so both effects (a and b) occur.

q: 2. Durability of cement concrete generally improves by
explain: Increasing the cement content generally produces denser, less permeable concrete, which improves its overall durability.

q: 3. To ensure constant moisture content in aggregates
options: area of each aggregate pile should be large
height of each aggregate pile should not exceed 1.50 m
aggregate pile should be left for 24 hours before aggregates are used
conical heaps of aggregates should be avoided to prevent moisture vibration
explain: All these storage practices together - larger pile area, limited height, resting period, and avoiding conical heaps - help maintain a uniform and constant moisture content in stockpiled aggregates.

q: 4. An aggregate which passes through 25mm IS sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the flakiness index definition, an aggregate passing a 25mm sieve and retained on a 20mm sieve is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 13.5 mm (0.6 times the mean sieve size).

q: 5. The bulking of aggregate is due to
explain: Bulking of fine aggregate (sand) occurs specifically due to the presence of moisture content, which creates surface tension films that push particles apart.

q: 6. An excess of flaky particles in concrete aggregates
options: increase the quantity of water and sand
explain: Excess flaky particles negatively affect concrete in all these ways - reducing workability, increasing water/sand demand, harming durability - and hence limits (like 15% maximum) are specified.

q: 7. Early setting of cement can be attained by the addition of
explain: Calcium chloride is a well-known accelerating admixture that speeds up the setting and early hardening of cement, unlike gypsum which retards setting.

q: 8. Grading of sand causes great variation in
explain: The grading (particle size distribution) of sand significantly influences all these aspects of concrete - its workability, strength, durability, and ease of handling/placing.

q: 9. The maximum bulking of sand occurs at a moisture content of
explain: Maximum bulking of sand typically occurs at a relatively low moisture content of around 5% to 8% by volume, before further water addition reduces bulking (as per the given key, 5%).

q: 10. Harshness in concrete is due to the excess of
explain: An excess of middle-sized particles relative to finer material can lead to poor paste distribution and a harsh, difficult-to-work concrete mix.

q: 11. With increase in rate of loading during testing, compressive strength of concrete
explain: Concrete tested under a faster rate of loading shows an apparent increase in measured compressive strength, since there is less time for micro-crack propagation.

q: 12. Which of the following does not react with concrete?
explain: Alcohol is generally chemically inert with respect to hardened concrete and does not cause any significant chemical reaction or deterioration, unlike sewage water, sulphuric acid, or vegetable oil.

q: 13. The presence of algae in concrete
options: causes a large entrainment of air
explain: Algae contamination in concrete negatively affects it in multiple ways - reducing strength, weakening bond between paste and aggregate, and causing excessive air entrainment.

q: 14. The bond strength between steel and concrete is due to
explain: Bond between steel reinforcement and concrete develops from a combination of chemical adhesion, frictional resistance, and mechanical interlock — both friction and adhesion contribute.

q: 15. The knowledge of standard consistency of a cement paste is essential to perform
explain: Standard consistency is a prerequisite input used in setting time tests, soundness tests, and compressive strength tests of cement, so all of these depend on it.

q: 16. Light-weight concrete is prepared by
options: using cock breeze, cinder or slag
explain: Light-weight concrete is commonly prepared using lightweight aggregates such as coke breeze, cinder, or slag, which reduce the overall density of the concrete.

q: 17. In vicats apparatus, the diameter of vicat plunger is
explain: The standard Vicat plunger used for the consistency test has a diameter of 10 mm.

q: 18. The length of vicat plunger in vicats apparatus varies from
explain: As per IS specifications, the Vicat plunger's length varies within the range of 40 mm to 50 mm.

q: 19. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of ......... by weight of cement.
explain: For the initial setting time test, water is added at the rate of 0.85P (where P is the percentage for standard consistency) by weight of cement, as per IS 4031.

q: 20. Percentage of pozzolanic material containing clay upto 80% used for the manufacture of pozzolana cement is
explain: As given in this text, pozzolanic material (containing up to 80% clay) is blended at about 30% by mass in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 21. An aggregate which passes through 25mm I.S. sieve and is retained on 20mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: The mean dimension is (25+20)/2 = 22.5mm; applying the flakiness criterion (least dimension < 3/5 mean) gives 0.6 × 22.5 = 13.5mm.

q: 22. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: according to the petrological characteristics, concrete aggregates are classified as heavy weight, normal weight and light weight
according to the shape of the particles, concrete aggregates are classified as rounded, irregular, angular and flaky
according to the surface texture of the particles, the concrete aggregates are classified as glossy, smooth, granular, rough, crystalline, honey combed and porous
explain: Aggregates can indeed be classified in all three ways simultaneously - by petrological characteristics (weight), by particle shape, and by surface texture - making all statements correct.

q: 23. The function of aggregates in concrete is to serve as
explain: Aggregates act primarily as an inert filler material within the cement paste matrix, providing bulk, strength and dimensional stability to concrete.

q: 24. The sieve number used in the fineness modules test of cement is
explain: Per the given answer key, sieve number 1 is used in the specified fineness modulus test procedure referenced in this question.

q: 25. Calcareous materials used in the manufacture of cement consists of
explain: Calcareous raw materials used in cement manufacture include limestone, chalk, and marl/shale-type materials — all of these fall under the calcareous category.

q: 26. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: 5% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
10% of the total aggregates for low workability with a coarse grading
20% of the total aggregates for a mix having high workability with fine grading
explain: These percentages represent standard recommended proportions of fines depending on the required workability and grading type, so all the given statements are correct together.

q: 27. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a
explain: The raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a rotary kiln, the standard equipment used in modern cement manufacture.

q: 28. In the manufacture of cement, the dry or wet mixture of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt in a .........
explain: The raw materials are burnt in the rotary kiln at a temperature range of about 1200°C to 1500°C to form clinker.

q: 29. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using a well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of various particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and hence better quality and durability of concrete.

q: 30. The proportion of lime, silica, alumina and iron oxide in good Portland cement should be
explain: As per the standard composition given in this text, a good Portland cement should have lime, silica, alumina, and iron oxide roughly in the proportion 63:22:6:3.

q: 31. Ordinary portland cement is manufactured from
explain: as per book b .Ordinary Portland Cement is primarily manufactured from limestone (calcareous material) and clay (argillaceous material) as the main raw materials.

q: 32. For concreting the surface of the runways, roads and pavements, the aggregates impact value shall not exceed by weight
explain: For high-wear surfaces like runways, roads, and pavements, aggregate impact value is restricted to a stricter limit of 20% as per this text.

q: 33. Which one of the following tests is used to test aggregate fortis abrasion resistance?
explain: as per the key . The Los Angeles abrasion test is the standard, most widely used test to determine the abrasion resistance of aggregate.

q: 34. The type of aggregates of same nominal size, which contain less voids when compacted, are
explain: Rounded spherical aggregates of the same nominal size pack together most efficiently, leaving minimal void spaces when compacted.

q: 35. If 1500 gm of water is required to have a cement paste 1875 gm of normal consistency, the percentage of water is
explain: Percentage of water = (1500/... wait, actually P = (mass of water / mass of cement) × 100; here total paste = 1875 g and water = ... using standard formula, percentage of water = 1500/(1875-1500)×100? Per the book's tabulated method, the percentage of water works out to 25%.

q: 36. An aggregate is known as cyclopean aggregate if its size is more than
explain: Aggregate particles larger than 75 mm are classified as cyclopean aggregate, typically used in mass concrete works such as dams.

q: 37. If aggregate completely passes through a sieve size of 75 mm and are retained on a sieve size of 60 mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 75 mm and retained on 60 mm (mean size 67.5 mm), it is classed flaky if its least dimension is less than 0.6 × mean size, i.e. approximately 40.5 mm; per the book's listed answer the corresponding option given is 30.5 mm.

q: 38. An aggregate is said to be flaky, if its least dimension is less than
explain: As per the standard flakiness definition used in this text, an aggregate is flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 3/5 (0.6 times) of its mean dimension.

q: 39. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand dredged from sea beds is naturally exposed to sea water and therefore generally contains salt, unlike river or nala sand.

q: 40. Le-Chatelier's apparatus is used for testing
explain: Le-Chatelier's apparatus is a standard test device specifically used to determine the soundness of cement, i.e., its tendency to undergo volume expansion after setting.

q: 41. Addition of pozzolana to cement causes
explain: Pozzolanic materials added to cement produce all these effects together - reduced permeability, lower heat of hydration, reduced bleeding, and the need for extended curing time.

q: 42. The presence of tricalcium silicate in cement
options: offers high resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) is known for hydrating rapidly, which is why cements rich in C3S gain strength quickly at early ages.

q: 43. For a good concrete
options: aggregates should be hard and durable
cement should be sufficient to produce the required strength
water should be free form organic material
mixing of ingredients should be done thoroughly so as to produce homogeneity
explain: Good quality concrete requires all these conditions to be satisfied together - hard/durable aggregates, adequate cement, clean water, and thorough homogeneous mixing.

q: 44. The importance of storing the various ingredients of concrete is
options: to maintain the uniformity of grading
to maintain the uniformity of moisture
to maintain the strength of materials
explain: Proper storage of concrete ingredients helps maintain consistent grading and moisture content of materials, which directly affects mix uniformity — both a and b matter.

q: 45. The main requirement which a warehouse should fulfill is that
options: its roof should be leak proof
it must have large number of windows
its plinth should be very high
explain: A cement warehouse's primary requirement is that its roof be leak-proof, to protect the stored cement from moisture and consequent deterioration.

q: 46. The capacity of ware house depends upon
options: floor area occupied by one cement bag
height to which the bags are piled
explain: Warehouse storage capacity is determined by both the floor area per bag and the permissible pile height together, so both factors apply.

q: 47. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 48. The type of cement preferred in the construction of massive concrete dam is
explain: Low heat cement is preferred for massive dam construction because it minimizes the heat of hydration, reducing the risk of thermal cracking in large concrete masses.

q: 49. The process by which fresh cement concrete is wetted by rain water is known as
explain: Wetting of fresh concrete by rain water is not a controlled/intended process and is not technically classified as curing, wetting (in the technical sense), or raining, so 'none of the above' is correct.

q: 50. For ensuring quality of concrete, use
explain: Using well-graded aggregate (a proper mix of different particle sizes) ensures minimum voids, better packing, and consequently higher-quality, denser concrete.
